hero.title: Elysia Engine
hero.desc: Elysia Engine is the personal engine branch I am shaping around rendering fundamentals, tooling clarity, and elegant iteration speed. This page is the first standalone shell for its architecture, milestones, and future graphics experiments.
hero.status_value: Scaffolding the first public page and system plan.

overview.intent_body: This project is meant to become a more authored engine space than a generic archive page. The goal is to explain the engine as a signature work: what it is trying to become, how it is organized, and why each system exists.
overview.focus_body: The first milestone is a clean bootstrap: app loop, renderer shell, scene flow, and a debug-friendly structure that will survive later rendering experiments.

rendering.title: Understand the pipeline, don't hide it
rendering.body: The renderer should stay readable enough that each stage can be studied, profiled, and replaced without losing the mental model.

tools.title: Build debugging into the engine early
tools.body: Debug overlays, scene inspection, and frame stats should be part of the engine shell instead of late add-ons.

structure.title: Prefer clean seams over premature scale
structure.body: The first versions should stay small, but the subsystems need enough separation to avoid redoing the whole project later.

identity.title: Give the project a voice, not just features
identity.body: This page frames the engine as a signature project with its own visual language, goals, and documentation rhythm.

renderer.title: Renderer Core
renderer.body: A dedicated page for frame flow, render passes, materials, and future backend work.

scene.title: Scene System
scene.body: A dedicated page for transforms, object ownership, scene graph direction, and runtime-to-render bridging.

tooling.title: Tooling
tooling.body: A dedicated page for debug panels, live controls, inspectors, and developer experience.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.body: A dedicated page for milestone planning, sequencing, risks, and representative-project framing.

app.title: App / Platform Layer
app.body: Window creation, input routing, frame pacing, and the bootstrap path that keeps the engine launch flow predictable.

renderer.title: Renderer Core
renderer.body: A focused rendering shell for command submission, camera data, render passes, materials, and future backend experiments.

scene.title: Scene / Entity Flow
scene.body: A light scene structure for transforms, object ownership, and the path between gameplay objects and renderer data.

tooling.title: Tooling / Diagnostics
tooling.body: Debug panels, live tuning, and future asset inspection pages that make iteration smoother while the engine is still changing rapidly.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap the shell
bootstrap.body: Stabilize project layout, startup flow, renderer ownership, and the first debug surfaces.
bootstrap.deliverable: Deliverable: a clean engine app that opens, renders a frame, and exposes core debug state.

rendering.title: First rendering milestone
rendering.body: Add a usable camera, mesh submission, material inputs, and an intentionally small but dependable pass layout.
rendering.deliverable: Deliverable: basic scene rendering with room for lighting and model-loading expansion.

tooling.title: Tooling and quality-of-life
tooling.body: Layer in performance counters, toggles, scene inspection, and the notes needed to explain the engine publicly.
tooling.deliverable: Deliverable: a better developer experience and a stronger case-study narrative.

renderer.title: Renderer bootstrap note
renderer.body: This slot is reserved for the first write-up covering initialization flow, ownership boundaries, and frame startup.

assets.title: Asset path note
assets.body: This slot can document how models, textures, and future materials move through the engine without creating fragile dependencies.

debug.title: Debug surface note
debug.body: This slot can explain debug overlays, live tuning controls, and how the engine exposes information while still being built.

page_renderer.title: Elysia Engine Renderer
page_renderer.heading: Renderer Core
page_renderer.desc: This page is reserved for the rendering path: frame flow, pass organization, camera data, materials, and future backend experiments.

scope.pipeline_body: Document the submit-update-render-present path and explain where each render stage lives.
scope.material_body: Track how shader parameters, textures, and mesh state become renderer-facing commands.
scope.experiment_body: Reserve space for comparing future OpenGL, software rasterizer, or other backend branches.

page_scene.title: Elysia Engine Scene System
page_scene.heading: Scene System
page_scene.desc: This page is reserved for transforms, object ownership, scene organization, and the path from gameplay-side structures to render submission.

scope.transform_body: Explain local/world transforms, parent-child relationships, and how update order stays understandable.
scope.ownership_body: Reserve a place to document object lifetimes, scene registration, and shared runtime services.
scope.bridge_body: Describe how scene data becomes render data without tangling runtime logic directly into the renderer.

page_tooling.title: Elysia Engine Tooling
page_tooling.heading: Tooling
page_tooling.desc: This page is reserved for debug UI, inspectors, counters, live toggles, and the pieces that make the engine easier to iterate on.

scope.debug_body: Explain the shape of immediate-mode tools, windows, toggles, and live renderer controls.
scope.inspect_body: Reserve a place for scene state, asset metadata, and entity inspection flows.
scope.metrics_body: Track frame time, GPU or CPU timings, and the measurements that shape optimization decisions.

page_roadmap.title: Elysia Engine Roadmap
page_roadmap.heading: Roadmap
page_roadmap.desc: This page is reserved for milestones, major technical bets, and the sequence used to grow Elysia Engine into a more complete signature project.

scope.sequence_body: Explain what should be built first, what can wait, and which features are blocked by earlier systems.
scope.risk_body: Reserve space for performance, complexity, and dependency risks that could shift priorities.
scope.case_body: Use this page to tie technical work back into the broader representative-project story.
